context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Don't take the email for the orders lookup from the request. Require an authenticated session or verified token on this route and use the email from that identity, e.g. `const email = req.user.email; orders = await db.ordersCollection.find({ email })`. If the request contains a different email (`updatedEmail`), reject it with 403 unless the caller has an authorised role such as admin, and log that access. Put the same authentication and ownership check on every HTTP method of this route, including GET, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. Then only the Data Principal who owns the orders, or an authorised role, can read or change them, which meets the access-control requirement in Rule 6(1)(b).
